attribution.note: Marcus's own numbered premise in his own post. He mentions LeCun and Altman as agreeing, but the assertion is his.

semantics.note: 'Will not' is an unhedged forecast. The next premise ('not directly bring... to AGI') backs the model-specific reading that GPT-5 itself won't be AGI. The normalisation fits.

contract.note: Marcus gave no definition of AGI. The plain reading (broadly general human-level intelligence, judged on the released GPT-5 only) is ordinary and doesn't stretch his words either way. Release plus substantive evaluations is a reasonable early-resolution trigger.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own release announcement, dated Aug 7, 2025. It shows the system shipped, but says nothing on whether it is AGI.

Contemporaneous Guardian report: OpenAI's CEO said GPT-5 had not reached AGI and named missing capabilities such as continuous learning. This is the explicit assessment the contract asks for, and it cuts against the company's own interest.

Independent METR evaluation found tasks that humans can do and GPT-5 failed for genuine capability reasons, plus limited autonomous time horizons. That corroborates material gaps, though it wasn't designed as an AGI test.
OpenAI's system card shows strong software-engineering scores. That is a single-domain strength and doesn't show broadly general human-level ability.

reviews.rationale: GPT-5 was released on Aug 7, 2025 (e1). An independent evaluation found genuine capability failures on tasks humans can do (e3). OpenAI's CEO said publicly that it had not reached AGI (e2). The contract's support condition is met. The strong coding results (e4) are domain-specific and don't amount to broadly general human-level capability. Nothing in the packet shows GPT-5 meeting the AGI reading.
